subject: Keystore / Vault inventory + short-term retention exception — triage
messages:

Cc: procurement@brightleafhealth.com
Date: 2026-08-03T09:18:00Z
Subject: Questions: keystore inventory, short retention for demo env

Hi Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our security team pulled together a quick set of follow-ups focused on key management and logs for the pilot environment. We want to confirm two things before we move forward with procurement:

1) Keystore inventory: do you have a single canonical list of customer-kept keys (BYOK/CMEK) vs Redwood-managed keys we can reference? Our auditors want the exact object IDs and rotation policy (if managed by Redwood).

2) Short-term retention exception: for the first 30 days of the pilot we need a temporary, 7-day ephemeral retention window for debug logs in the sandbox — is an exception path available (audit evidence + attestation) while we finalize retention SLOs?

I attached the BLH_Audit_Qs.xlsx with line items. Can you loop in whoever owns the keystore inventory and telemetry evidence?

Appreciate a quick triage so our procurement team can keep to the timeline.

—Anne

Hi Anne —

Thanks for the clear list. Looping in Ben (platform/instrumentation) and Grace (product/compliance) to cover keystore inventory and an evidence path for a limited retention exception. Quick answers up front:

- Canonical inventory: we maintain a per-customer keystore manifest (object ids, type: BYOK vs Redwood-managed, last-rotation timestamp) — I can export a sanitized CSV for BrightLeaf.
- Short-term retention exception: we can support a constrained, time-boxed 7-day ephemeral window in a sandbox under an evidence-runbook. It requires an acceptance attestation from your security owner + an internal exceptions ticket so we log the decision and retention SLA.

Proposed triage tasks (owners):
- Ben: provide telemetry artifacts and an export of the keystore manifest (redwood-keystore-inventory.csv).
- Grace: outline the exception attestation template + required evidence items.
- Tessa: confirm whether the sandbox will run on a Dedicated pool (impacts isolation) and list any networking constraints.

Timeline: can we aim to deliver the manifest + evidence checklist by EOD Wednesday (2026-08-04)? If that works we'll attach the artifacts to the DocuSign package for procurement.

Marcus Lin
Director, Security Engineering | Redwood Inference

+1 on the plan. Quick technical notes from instrumentation/ops:

- Inventory export: I will generate a sanitized CSV that includes: key_id, key_type (BYOK/CMEK/Redwood), customer_id, last_rotation_utc, kms_provider. We will redact material that would violate other customers' confidentiality. Expect redwood-keystore-inventory.csv in ~3 hours.

- Telemetry for evidence: for the exception path we can provide: token-level request traces, per-request keystore usage counts, and a compact audit timeline (UTC) for any access to customer keys during the window. We do not ship raw key material.

- Sandbox retention behavior: ops can toggle a short TTL for sandbox logs via config flag (sandbox.log.ttl_days). Caveat: if sandbox is on Dedicated hardware we need a maintenance window to flip the flag to avoid impacting other tenants sharing the management plane.

Questions for Anne: can you confirm whether the sandbox will be in our Hosted trial or on a Dedicated instance? That changes the rollback and evidence capture steps.

Thanks all — sketching the product/compliance asks and acceptance criteria so we have a concrete checklist: 

1) Keystore manifest export (Ben). Acceptance: CSV with key_id, key_role, provider, rotation_date, and confirmation of whether key is customer-managed or Redwood-managed. Redactions allowed for multi-tenant fields.

2) Evidence package for 7-day sandbox TTL exception. Acceptance:
   - Attestation template signed by customer security owner (we provide a template)
   - Audit timeline for the TTL window (UTC) with request-level traces for any key access events
   - Proof of sandbox isolation (namespace + cluster id) and confirmation of retention toggle performed by Redwood ops

3) Risk mitigations:
   - Exception will be timeboxed and logged in our exceptions tracker with an owner and auto-expiry (no manual extension without review).
   - No key material will be exported; only metadata and access logs are shared.

4) Rollout note: If BrightLeaf requests the sandbox on Dedicated capacity, we require a 48-hour ops lead time to schedule the config change and to ensure the evidence artifacts are captured from the right control plane.

Deliverables ETA: Ben's CSV + a draft attestation template from me by EOD 2026-08-04; final evidence package by 2026-08-05 if sandbox environment details are confirmed today.

Grace O'Connor
Product Manager, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
